evidence.quote:
For Ernie Lane had stopped walking
hurriedly past that extra door, had stopped giving it only casual
curiosity, had even stopped wondering afterward.
evidence.paraphrase: An extra door in the house appears and disappears, prompting Ernie's growing attention.

evidence.quote:
He felt the refinished wall, his fingertips searching for hidden
panels. There was none.
evidence.paraphrase: Ernie physically investigates the wall to find a hidden explanation for the vanishing door.

evidence.quote:
He was not a man of hallucinations. He was
not a victim of superstition, fear or near-sightedness. He only wanted
to know why he saw a door one day and didn't see it the next.
evidence.paraphrase: Ernie asserts his rationality and seeks a logical reason for the door's inconsistent appearance.

evidence.quote:
"Darling, don't call me
Melinee when my name is Marsha. It just isn't done."
evidence.paraphrase: Ernie's wife shifts between being Melinee (blonde) and Marsha (red-haired), a change tied to the house.

evidence.quote:
Melinee? It was all like a breath of spring. Away from that house, she
was a different person.
evidence.paraphrase: The narration contrasts the wife's identity away from the house versus inside it.

evidence.quote:
The pale green wall of the hallway confronted him. It was as if the
door were merely hinged onto the wall. No opening whatever.
evidence.paraphrase: The extra door opens onto solid wall with no opening behind it.

evidence.quote:
It was as if the
wall were twelve inches thick--as if
he were not hearing anything at all--and yet hearing.
evidence.paraphrase: Ernie hears voices that seem to come from behind a wall where nothing should be.

evidence.quote:
The dimensions immediately struck Ernie as all wrong. It was far bigger
than the hall closet where it was supposed to be.
evidence.paraphrase: The concealed space is impossibly larger than the physical closet that should contain it.

evidence.quote:
The
whole thing seemed to be about thirty degrees lopsided.
evidence.paraphrase: The hidden room's floor is tilted about thirty degrees.

evidence.quote:
It turned his mind, his body, wrong-side out. Like the
squeezing out of a wet mop by a steamroller.
evidence.paraphrase: Passing through the opening physically distorts Ernie as he crosses into the other space.

evidence.quote:
"Kronkite,
Ernie here says we are thirty degrees off. Can you shift the
equilibrium?
evidence.paraphrase: A technician is asked to adjust the equilibrium of the dimension to correct its tilt.

evidence.quote:
"This is your house, of course, but we're not quite there yet. We're in
what you would call--oh, another dimension."
evidence.paraphrase: Ernie's host explains they are in another dimension coincident with his house.

evidence.quote:
"Oh, you and I have lived in the same vicinity all our lives,
even crossed each other's paths, but we are in different
dimensions--different worlds in the same place."
evidence.paraphrase: The host describes overlapping dimensions occupying the same space with parallel people.

evidence.quote:
What we are
both in is a third realm sponsored by the government--the federal
government of The Unison States. Congrice sponsored this scientific
investigation
evidence.paraphrase: The setting is an experimental third dimension funded by a parallel-world government's scientific program.

evidence.quote:
"Melinee in your dimension, Marsha in ours. You and she exist in our
dimension as well. Same types, same characteristics inwardly. But not
the same outwardly."
evidence.paraphrase: The host explains that people exist in both dimensions with the same inner nature but different outward forms.

evidence.quote:
"Our object, of course, is to start out the new dimension with an Adam
and Eve," the host said.
evidence.paraphrase: The experiment's goal is to populate a new dimension starting with Ernie and Marsha as founders.

evidence.quote:
we will install a series of
transitional burnouts. These will break down molecular resistance which
our more powerful equipment creates on solid portions of your house.
evidence.paraphrase: The host describes using transitional burnouts to break down molecular resistance to align the dimension with the house.

evidence.quote:
"The extra door in the hallways? Sooner or later she
will see it, wonder as you did and open it. This time we will have the
magnetic field force turned on.
evidence.paraphrase: The door is a magnetic field-force entrance intended to pull people into the dimension.

evidence.quote:
there was a technical miscalculation in our instruments
which, while allowing you to enter this new dimension, also did not
allow you to enter.
evidence.paraphrase: A miscalculation produced a paradox in which Ernie both entered and did not enter the dimension.

evidence.quote:
For when the other you enters our hallway
door, we shall have to do away with one of you.
evidence.paraphrase: The duplication error means one of the two Ernies must be eliminated.

evidence.quote:
slung bottle after
bottle at the instruments, caused three small explosions, a sputtering
red fire, a terrible burst of black smoke and a sudden explosion that
turned the whole new dimension--such as it was--into a white blinding
sun.
evidence.paraphrase: Ernie destroys the experimental equipment, causing explosions that obliterate the new dimension.

evidence.quote:
walked to a little white
building near the Washingable Monument, stepped inside, handed a man
his Other World card, then walked through a door, felt sick at his
stomach, came out to the streetcar line to Melinee and home.
evidence.paraphrase: Ernie uses a pass to travel through a door between dimensions back to his own world and home.

evidence.quote: "There was an explosion in the night. I think it was gas escaping."
evidence.paraphrase: Ernie explains the night's events to his wife as an ordinary gas explosion.

evidence.quote: "He says his name is Irvin--"
evidence.paraphrase: A duplicate of Ernie, named Irvin, arrives at the door, realizing the feared doubling.
